LSE 0.5.5 decodes 10 to 12% faster (6% with MTP=3), answers short prompts sooner, and answers the first request at each prompt size up to twice as fast. On macOS with mac_linuxgpu v0.1.161 (build 265) it keeps HRX kernel arguments in VRAM. Loading takes longer, because the server now prepares its kernels before it reports ready.

**Requires mac_linuxgpu v0.1.151 (build 255) or later** on macOS. Kernel arguments in VRAM need **v0.1.161 (build 265)**. With an older driver, LSE keeps kernel arguments in host memory, as 0.5.4 did. If a driver has the build-265 BAR-write interface but refuses it, GPU setup fails with an error; LSE does not fall back to host kernel arguments. The measurements below were taken on v0.1.161 (build 265), with 0.5.4 measured on the same driver.

**Load time and memory.** The server makes every request shape's kernels resident before it reports ready. With the kernel cache on disk, the pinned DFlash2 configuration now loads in 9.8 s instead of 4.1 s, and plain decoding in 8.6 s instead of 3.0 s. The host memory footprint at ready is 610 MB instead of 384 MB with DFlash2. The first launch of a new LSE build, with none of its kernels in the cache, compiles them before it reports ready: 112 s with DFlash2 on this machine. 0.5.4 compiled them during the first requests instead.

## Changes

1. **Faster decode.** The single-row 4-bit decode contraction issues all of a column's weight, scale and bias reads before it stages the activations. Partial RoPE rotates in one launch, one-token passes reshape heads instead of transposing them, and a decode row's GDN q/k preparation is one launch: 352 fewer launches per plain decode token. A plain 640-token decode runs at 31.7 tok/s, up from 28.8 (+10.3%).
2. **Faster speculative decoding.** The 8-row down projection widens each weight word with one shift and one mask per operand register. A vocabulary-projection wave owns four columns at 6 to 8 rows, so a verify pass or DFlash2 draft reads each activation run once for all four. A 4-row MTP=3 verify pass runs its gate and up projections as one fused SwiGLU launch. A DFlash2 draft's 8-row 8-bit projections read one shared activation panel per input. A 640-token decode runs at 57.2 tok/s with DFlash2, up from 51.2 (+11.8%), and 55.5 tok/s with MTP=3, up from 52.2 (+6.3%).
3. **Shorter time to first token for short prompts.** 4-bit GEMMs of 65 to 767 rows are tiled from 48x32 wave tiles, so one row tile holds a whole pass of up to 192 rows. `loom-vmem-load-latency.patch` gives loomc's AMDGPU schedule the real global-load latency, so the GEMM issues its loads ahead of the math that waits on them. Warm TTFT: 137 tokens 0.128 s, 43 ms saved (+34%); 271 tokens 0.207 s, 74 ms saved (+36%); 646 tokens 0.444 s, 50 ms saved (+11%); 2118 tokens 1.319 s, 132 ms saved (+10%).
4. **The first request at a new size runs at warm speed.** Its kernels are already resident, so it no longer emits and loads them between launches. They load together as one code object per shape set, about 260 executables instead of about 4000. First request at each size: 137 tokens 0.196 s, 169 ms saved (+86%); 271 tokens 0.210 s, 231 ms saved (+110%); 1060 tokens 0.695 s, 458 ms saved (+66%).
5. **HRX kernel arguments in VRAM.** `gfx120x-hdp-kernarg-publication.patch` (the change in ROCm/hrx-system#1331) admits RDNA4 to HRX's VRAM kernel-argument path on the macOS and Linux builds. On macOS, `hsa-bar-write-bracket.patch` opts into the build-265 runtime's BAR writes and brackets each submission's stores into the GPU's BARs under the driver's gate, so a power transition, reset or Disconnect GPU never meets a store in flight. Measured during development, on build 265: plain decode 30.7 to 31.8 tok/s and DFlash2 53.0 to 54.2 tok/s; on Linux with ROCm 7.13, DFlash2 +4.9 to +7.5% and plain +2.2 to +3.7%. The iOS framework does not apply these two patches and keeps kernel arguments in host memory.
6. **RDNA4 matrix-core tools.** `scripts/rdna4-matrix` holds standalone matrix-core microbenchmarks and an FP8 Q4 prefill GEMM prototype.

Greedy (temperature 0) output on the pinned configuration is identical to 0.5.4 with DFlash2 and plain decoding.

## Performance

Qwen3.8-27B Q4 with the Q8 DFlash2 draft on an R9700, mac_linuxgpu v0.1.161 (build 265), `--batch-size 1024 --ubatch-size 1024 --kv-cache-dtype bf16 --kv-len 262100`, `LSE_REQUIRE_DEVICE_KERNELS=1`. Cold is the first request of that size after the server starts, with the kernel cache on disk. Warm is the median of five requests that follow five more at the same size. Decode is the median of five 640-token runs after one more.

| Prompt tokens | Warm TTFT | Warm prefill | Cold TTFT | 0.5.4 warm TTFT | 0.5.4 cold TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 137 | 0.128 s | 1,070 tok/s | 0.196 s | 0.171 s | 0.365 s |
| 271 | 0.207 s | 1,309 tok/s | 0.210 s | 0.281 s | 0.441 s |
| 532 | 0.385 s | 1,382 tok/s | 0.389 s | 0.427 s | 0.697 s |
| 646 | 0.444 s | 1,455 tok/s | 0.449 s | 0.494 s | 0.734 s |
| 1060 | 0.677 s | 1,566 tok/s | 0.695 s | 0.697 s | 1.153 s |
| 2118 | 1.319 s | 1,606 tok/s | 1.347 s | 1.451 s | 1.804 s |
| 4230 | 2.643 s | 1,600 tok/s | 2.644 s | 2.732 s | 2.865 s |

| Mode | 640-token decode | Draft acceptance | 2K prompt (2406 tokens) | 4K prompt (4787 tokens) | 0.5.4, 640-token decode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash2 | 57.2 tok/s | 65.5% | 58.5 tok/s, TTFT 1.52 s | 65.8 tok/s, TTFT 3.05 s | 51.2 tok/s |
| MTP=3 (`--mtp qwen38-27b-mtp-q8 --mtp-depth 3`) | 55.5 tok/s | 68.9% | 59.0 tok/s | — | 52.2 tok/s |
| Plain (`--dflash2=off`) | 31.7 tok/s | — | 31.6 tok/s, TTFT 1.50 s | — | 28.8 tok/s |

Model load, launch to ready with the checkpoint in the file cache and the kernel cache on disk: 9.8 s with DFlash2, 8.6 s plain, 3.9 s with MTP (0.5.4: 4.1, 3.0 and 3.2 s). 0.5.5 prepares every request shape's kernels before it reports ready. Host memory footprint at ready with DFlash2: 610 MB (0.5.4: 384 MB). The first launch of a new LSE build, with none of its kernels in the cache, compiles them before it reports ready: 112 s with DFlash2 on this machine.
